sd_khayyam_spire.blurb: Khayyam Spire is a 320-foot granite tower in the Needles of Custer State Park, the first big formation you meet when hiking the Cathedral Spires trail. Its bright yellow west and south faces make it easy to pick out. All twelve climbs here are traditional: a couple of moderate lines around 5.6 to 5.9, then a steep jump into serious 5.11 and 5.12 territory with one 5.13. The cracks are long and sustained, and several routes take multiple pitches, so expect a full day with a rack and two ropes. It suits experienced trad parties rather than beginners, and descent is by rappel.

sd_near_downs.blurb: Near Downs is a granite fin in the Middle Earth section of the Needles, up behind Sylvan Lake in Custer State Park, and is the highest of the ridgelines there. It has a north-west face and a south-east face, and mostly holds trad lines with a pair of bolted sport routes. Ten of the twelve climbs are trad. Grades start near 5.8, build through 5.10, and finish with a cluster at 5.12 featuring hard cracks such as the off-width on the south side. Some routes finish at an anchor needing a rappel. A good pick for confident trad climbers who want a quiet, adventurous day among granite pinnacles.

sd_wild_west_wall.blurb: Wild West Wall is a small sport crag at the far end of The Dark Side in Spearfish Canyon, on top of a rock pillar close to a gated tunnel. The twelve bolted routes run from 5.10 into the 5.12s, with most of them at 5.12, so it rewards climbers who already lead the grade. It is reached by hiking the steep trail up to The Dark Side, then following the road left rather than right. Routes here are newer and some lines are still being added. Plan on a quiet day away from the busier canyon walls, combined with a visit to the neighbouring Dark Side wall.

sd_campground_boulder.blurb: Campground Boulder is a big granite block above the trail on the far side of Sylvan Lake in Custer State Park, with a tall yellow face looking out toward the water. John Gill left classic lines here, and it is often called one of the best boulders in the state. All twelve problems are bouldering, spanning from V0 to a single V9, though most fall between V2 and V4. Expect mantles, flakes, edging and delicate friction, plus high lines that are best top-roped from the bolted anchors if you lack pads and spotters. Short walk from the lake, and a worthwhile stop on any Sylvan Lake bouldering day.
